message.text: On macOS, the read grant and environment a probe runs under now depend on the host's git lookup, `sandbox.git()` → `probeGit`. That lookup decides whether git's program, exec path, share directory and system configuration are readable, whether `<scratch>/git` goes on `PATH`, and whether `GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM=1` is set. The probing environment that goes into the lens request key holds only writer, trustWriters, timeout, `probe.read`, `conditions` and `probingHost`. `probingHost` is still platform, sandbox kind, sandboxVersion, arch and node, and the git lookup's outcome is in none of them. The head decision's Keys section leaves 'where the developer tools live' out of the key. In practice that leaves out whether git can run in a probe at all.

Choice: every run's selection, the first and the one a quick run escalates to, names its whole probing environment as one JSON value, so any change to its writer, the policy's word, its time limit, its grant or its host runs it again. The host is one value: the sandbox's platform and kind, and the CPU architecture and version of the Node that runs the probes. The coordinator chose that on 2026-11-14, applying the shared-record decision the maintainer adopted on 2026-11-13, that a check's request holds its host facts. The probing protocol also holds what Melian's probe runner gives a probe, over fixed paths, which the coordinator chose on 2026-11-14 under the same decision. [The identity guideline](../guidelines/identity.md) lists what about the host and the runner is left out, and why. The planner's decisions at base and its earlier findings leave the instruction fingerprint, as the caller-context decision kept caller context out, and stay in the prompt. That exclusion was a builder's choice; the maintainer accepted it on 2026-11-13, in the coordinator's session, after a host round at `4f83a8a6` raised it. The fingerprint holds the probing protocol as the build renders it, so a Melian release that changes it runs the level again: each role tool's name, description and schema, the fixed limits, and the table of every fixed wording the planner and the prober read, the planner's role and context among them. The prompt functions build their text from that table and hold no wording of their own, so every branch of each counts, and a test fails when one does. The verifier's version hashes the wording it reads of a claim's probe, a table of its own, the same way. Beside each table, each key hashes its prompts as `probingRenderings` renders them over fixed samples, one for each branch the render functions hold, so a change in how a prompt is put together, its order, separators or quoting, runs the level again or judges stored claims again. The maintainer ruled on that on 2026-11-13, in the coordinator's se [cut at 2 KiB]
- The selection names a probing run's whole environment, so a review under another writer, policy word, time limit, grant or host never attaches to a live run, and now never copies a finished one.

explanation.what: On macOS, the read grant and environment a probe runs under now depend on the host's git lookup, `sandbox.git()` → `probeGit`. That lookup decides whether git's program, exec path, share directory and system configuration are readable, whether `<scratch>/git` goes on `PATH`, and whether `GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM=1` is set. The probing environment that goes into the lens request key holds only writer, trustWriters, timeout, `probe.read`, `conditions` and `probingHost`. `probingHost` is still platform, sandbox kind, sandboxVersion, arch and node, and the git lookup's outcome is in none of them. The head decision's Keys section leaves 'where the developer tools live' out of the key. In practice that leaves out whether git can run in a probe at all.
explanation.whatToDo: Add the outcome of the git lookup to `probingHost`, or to the probing environment next to `conditions`. Do not key the paths. Key the kind of answer: unavailable (with the reason's class), linked, or linked with no system configuration. Then a host whose git becomes usable, or stops being usable, or gains or loses a system configuration, runs the probing lens again. `openHeadProbe`'s host check would then also refuse a resumed run whose git state has moved. Leaving it out instead needs an explicit amendment of the attach-key decision.
explanation.whyHere: The active base attach-key decision says a probing run's selection names its whole environment, 'so any change to its writer, the policy's word, its time limit, its grant or its host runs it again'. The finished-probing-runs decision keeps that clause: 'a review under another writer, policy word, time limit, grant or host never attaches to a live run, and now never copies a finished one.' This change makes the grant depend on host state the key never sees, so a run made with git unavailable keeps being reused after git becomes available, and the reverse. A failed git call exits non-zero, which `probeConclusive` counts as conclusive, so the stale run passes `runStands` and is copied. The reasons the base text gives for leaving things out (installed dependencies, what the read paths hold, the runner's code, filesystem case, OS release) do not cover whether a grant is given at all. The head decision makes this new exclusion itself, with no Amends or Supersedes of the attach-key decision.

properties.failureScenario: A reviewer on macOS has Command Line Tools with Apple Git older than 2.42 (for example 2.39). `git var GIT_CONFIG_SYSTEM` fails there, so `probeGit` returns `{ unavailable }` (probe-git.ts:56-58). `Probe.open` grants no git reads and puts no git link on `PATH`. The probing lens reviews head H, and a probe that runs `git init`, or the `melian` CLI, fails with exit 1 because `/usr/bin/git`'s xcrun launcher cannot run in the sandbox. That result is conclusive, so the prober either reports a finding that rests on the host's missing git or closes the probe as wrongly written, and the run stands. The reviewer then updates Command Line Tools to Apple Git 2.50, so `probeGit` now returns `{ program, reads }` and probes can run git. The next `melian review` of H builds the same environment: same writer, policy, timeout, read, conditions, and a `probingHost` with the same platform, kind, sandboxVersion, arch and node. The request key therefore matches, `runStands` holds, and the review attaches to or copies the old run. The finding that rests on missing git, or the clean result with no git attack, stays until the head changes. The reverse happens too: a run made where git worked, or where `/etc/gitconfig` was absent (`noSystem`) and is later created, is reused on a host whose probes would now see something else.
